Blockmediary is a documentary escrow and document-verification service. It is not a lending or financing product.
This workbook is an indicative university idea-presentation model, not a business-loan application, regulatory filing, legal opinion or investment commitment.
Amounts are readable planning approximations. Client funds remain safeguarded and excluded from operating cash, revenue and runway.
1. Edit blue inputs in Assumptions and Launch Readiness. Yellow cells are key presentation controls; formulas and linked values update automatically.
2. Assumptions!C4 selects commercial performance: 1=Low, 2=Base, 3=High. The delivered presentation default is Base.
3. Launch Readiness!B5 selects timing: 1=Early, 2=Base, 3=Delayed. The route is fixed as DIFC partner-led pilot followed by VARA expansion.
4. Startup 6mo holds core pre-revenue build costs. Launch Readiness separately times partner/DIFC pilot costs, future VARA fees and restricted capital.
5. P&L 5yr, Cash Flow Statement and Model Checks provide economics, runway and integrity; supporting tabs retain sources, sensitivities, risks and safeguarding detail.
Model base currency = GBP (£). USD-priced vendors (Anthropic, AWS, Vercel, KYC, gas) are converted at the FX rate in Assumptions (GBPUSD).
Driver Tables keeps each driver in its native quoted currency; the conversion happens where the driver feeds the P&L.

values: Tier Economics - revenue, cost and risk by document-intake tier

*Year-1 deal values (£35k Tier A; £30k Tier B/C) and 10%/8%/5% annual growth are triangulated planning averages, not observed tier-level transaction data. The research report documents the proxies, judgement and confidence limits.
**Take rates of 0.8%/1.5%/3.0% are management pricing choices informed by Tazapay, Truzo, XREX, Escrow.com and bank-LC comparables. They are paid-pilot hypotheses, not competitor quotations.

***Minimum fees (£150/£250/£500) are internal floors intended to protect contribution margin on smaller deals; no external tariff is being claimed. Validate conversion and willingness-to-pay in the pilot.

Presentation-grade assumptions requiring UAE counsel, regulated-partner confirmation or firm quotes before live use.
Why it's high-risk / what to confirm
The Month-12 pilot assumes a regulated partner can support the relevant custody/settlement permissions and approve the operating model. Responsibilities and customer limits remain unconfirmed.
VARA licensing perimeter for UAE-wide scale
The Month-30 scale case assumes the required VARA categories, capital and operating controls can be secured. Current model values are planning assumptions, not approval.
All revenue figures are 'estimate' quality — no clean public documentary-escrow comparable. The entire revenue model is a hypothesis until validated in paid pilots.
Bespoke contract governing on-chain release of funds against off-chain documents; enforceability across buyer/seller jurisdictions is untested.
Audit cost depends on final contract complexity; a contract holding client funds warrants a top-tier audit and possibly re-audit after changes.
UAE AML/KYC obligations and MLRO split
Internal compliance FTE owns controls; the MLRO/specialist retainer is advisory and escalation support. Partner responsibilities must be documented to avoid gaps or duplicate costs.
Trade documents may contain personal data. DIFC/UAE processing, transfer, retention and breach requirements must be mapped before pilot launch.
Crypto/fintech PI, cyber and D&O can be hard to place and carry heavy loadings or exclusions (e.g. crypto exclusions). Quotes will vary widely.
Ranges are benchmark-quality, not offers; actual hires may sit outside the band, especially scarce crypto/compliance talent.
The initial raise and later VARA capital call are modelled separately. Funding availability and investor timing may not match the planned launch milestones.
Core premise: Blockmediary releases against documents, not actual delivery/condition. Must be drafted explicitly in TEA and customer terms.
Retained risk: if our rules engine, examiner, API integration or release workflow makes a bad decision, we may face claims.
Carrier/eBL/API source may be unavailable or wrong; model includes fallback and integration costs.
Manual paper, courier, originals and forensics create higher operational error and dispute risk.
Need contracts with eBL, carrier API, forensics, courier and KYC providers to push source failures and direct costs outward.
Reserve is assumption-based, not actuarial. Must be revisited after pilot loss/dispute history.
Base planning assumes paid pilot Month 12 and VARA scale Month 30. Rework, partner conditions or regulator feedback can move both dates and increase operating funding need.
